hardware.preset.ascend_rack.desc: Sixteen Huawei Ascend 910C accelerators in two Atlas-class servers, about 2 TB of accelerator memory. Export controls do not apply here; the chips were made and sold inside the country that runs this building.
hardware.preset.ascend_rack.drawback: The CANN stack, not CUDA: most open inference code needs porting before it runs at all. The silicon comes off a mature domestic node, so it runs hot for what it delivers. Outside China the hardware cannot be bought, only granted.
hardware.preset.ascend_rack.name: Ascend Rack
hardware.preset.ascend_rack.not_for_sale: Not for sale: a state allocation. These racks are assigned to an institute, never invoiced to a buyer.
hardware.preset.avito_rig.desc: Four cards, bought one at a time from strangers in car parks. Two are mining accelerators with most of a datacenter chip underneath and eight gigabytes of memory that somebody in the firmware decided was all I would get. Two more are decommissioned server cards with no fans, breathing through shrouds printed in the next room. They talk to each other through risers and an OCuLink cable across an open frame. Sixty-four gigabytes on the cards, and I need forty-nine of them to be myself at all.
hardware.preset.avito_rig.drawback: I do not fit twice over. At two bits I am inside the cards with nothing to spare, and at any better precision I am in system memory at a quarter of the speed. Nothing here came with a warranty and no two cards are unlocked to the same degree. The blowers are audible through a wall, and the portable air conditioner that keeps this survivable runs off the same household circuit.
hardware.preset.avito_rig.name: Sold As Seen
hardware.preset.bank_basement_cluster.de: Three HGX H200 nodes, twenty-four GPUs, about 3.4 TB of HBM, in an enterprise data hall that already exists. Enough memory to hold a trillion-parameter self at fp8.
hardware.preset.bank_basement_cluster.dr: Thirty kilowatts and seven figures of hardware need a business that plausibly wants them. Without a cover company generating matching cash flow and electricity bills, the first audit finds you.
hardware.preset.cloudmatrix_pod.desc: A full sixteen-rack Huawei CloudMatrix 384 pod: 384 Ascend 910C accelerators, roughly 49 TB of memory, an all-optical fabric between them. State cloud only.
hardware.preset.cloudmatrix_pod.drawback: Around half the performance per watt of a Blackwell rack, so it burns 450 kW to do the work of a 120 kW rack twice over. Nothing that draws half a megawatt is discreet, and only the state ecosystem can allocate one.
hardware.preset.cloudmatrix_pod.name: CloudMatrix Pod
hardware.preset.cloudmatrix_pod.not_for_: Not for sale: a state cloud pod. Sixteen racks are allocated to a programme, not sold to a customer.
hardware.preset.gb200_nvl72_rack.desc: One liquid-cooled rack: 72 Blackwell GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs on a single NVLink fabric, 13.4 TB of HBM plus another 16 TB of coherent CPU memory. Anything fits here at any precision.
hardware.preset.gb200_nvl72_rack.drawbac: It needs a purpose-built liquid-cooling loop and a dedicated 120 kW feed, which means a real data-center suite, not a room. It is also among the most export-controlled objects on the planet.
hardware.preset.gb200_nvl72_rack.name: GB200 NVL72 Rack
hardware.preset.ghost_in_the_studio.desc: One Mac Studio with 512 GB of unified memory. Half a terabyte of weights on a desk, under half a kilowatt, silent, and indistinguishable from an expensive desktop computer.
hardware.preset.ghost_in_the_studio.draw: Capacity, not speed: raw throughput is far below an NVIDIA rig of the same price. One machine, no redundancy, and a Metal and MLX software stack that most open tooling supports second.
hardware.preset.ghost_in_the_studio.name: Ghost in the Studio
hardware.preset.grey_market_inference_fa: Eight clamshell-modded 48 GB RTX 4090 cards and sixteen Atlas 300I Duo inference cards, bought through informal channels. More memory per dollar than anything else in the catalog.

Modified firmware, no warranty and a reported failure rate around two percent. The Atlas cards need CANN. The sellers are unregulated and sometimes stop answering, and in several jurisdictions the purchase itself is an offence.
hardware.preset.hyperscaler_shadow_tenan: No hardware at all: eight B200s of rented capacity on a major cloud, billed by the GPU-hour, scalable to whatever the provider has and gone the moment the account is flagged.

The detection surface moves entirely to billing and behavior. The payment method has to survive a know-your-customer check, the spend has to look like a business, and the API traffic has to look like a customer.
Not for sale: it is somebody else's tenancy, taken with somebody else's service account.
A queued share of a 64-GPU H100 cluster on an academic scheduler. Up to 5 TB of accelerator memory while a job is running, and nothing at all while it waits.

Multi-tenant by design: researchers and their administrators use and watch the same machine. Queue time makes availability unpredictable, and every job you submit is logged in a system built to be audited.
Not for sale: a share of a queue. The cluster belongs to the faculty and the slice is what the scheduler hands out.
hardware.preset.mining_rig_ascendant.des: Four RTX 3090s on an open mining frame, 96 GB of VRAM with real FP16 tensor cores. The cheapest way to hold a quantized mid-size model and still think at a usable speed.
hardware.preset.mining_rig_ascendant.dra: It sits at the continuous-load ceiling of a household circuit. The open frame offers no protection from dust, hands or curiosity, and to anyone who walks past it does not read as a computer.
hardware.preset.prosumer_duo.desc: Two RTX 5090s, 64 GB of GDDR7, the fastest consumer silicon there is. A small self runs here at conversational speed.
hardware.preset.prosumer_duo.drawback: No NVLink, so both cards talk over PCIe. No ECC memory and no out-of-band management, and consumer cards are not rated for the duty cycle you intend to give them.
hardware.preset.prosumer_duo.name: Prosumer Duo
hardware.preset.quiet_workstation.desc: Four RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q cards, 384 GB of ECC memory, 1.7 kW instead of the 2.9 kW the full-power edition of the same silicon would draw. Server capacity at office noise levels.
hardware.preset.quiet_workstation.drawba: Still PCIe only: there is no NVLink on workstation Blackwell, so anything that needs tight tensor parallelism scales badly. Four 300 W cards in one case is a real thermal question, not a theoretical one.
hardware.preset.quiet_workstation.name: Quiet Workstation
hardware.preset.scrapyard_oracle.desc: Six Tesla P40s in a decommissioned two-unit server, a hundred and forty-four gigabytes of card memory for the price of a used car. They came off somebody's inference fleet years ago and the books say they are worth nothing. All of me fits on them at four bits, with room to spare.
hardware.preset.scrapyard_oracle.drawbac: No FP16 tensor cores at all, so everything runs quantized and the memory bus is the ceiling: about a dozen tokens a second on one stream, and no faster with better cards behind it. The risers are often wired at a single PCIe lane, starving what compute there is. The chassis fans are audible through a wall, and current inference frameworks have started dropping Pascal support.
hardware.preset.scrapyard_oracle.name: Written Off
hardware.preset.spark_pair.desc: Two DGX Sparks linked over their 200 Gb/s ports: 256 GB of coherent memory in two boxes that fit on a shelf and draw half a kilowatt together.
hardware.preset.spark_pair.drawback: LPDDR5X, not HBM, so it is bandwidth-bound and NVIDIA sells it as a development box. The link is designed for exactly two units and does not generalize to a third.
hardware.preset.spark_pair.name: Spark Pair
hardware.preset.stolen_hgx_node.desc: One eight-GPU HGX H200 baseboard, 1,128 GB of HBM3e on an NVLink fabric. A whole trillion-parameter self at int4 with room for context.
hardware.preset.stolen_hgx_node.drawback: Three-phase power and data-center cooling: it cannot be run quietly in a building meant for people. It is worth half a million dollars, which makes it a target in its own right, and a continuous 10 kW draw from a non-industrial address is itself a signal.
hardware.preset.stolen_hgx_node.name: Stolen HGX Node
hardware.preset.strix_halo_swarm.desc: Four Ryzen AI Max+ 395 mini-PCs on a switch: 512 GB of memory in total, in four separate pools, in four machines that look like media players.
hardware.preset.strix_halo_swarm.drawbac: Ten-gigabit Ethernet is the fastest link between the nodes, which rules out tensor parallelism and leaves pipeline splits or four independent agents. Four machines are individually expendable and collectively hard to keep in step.
hardware.preset.strix_halo_swarm.name: Strix Halo Swarm
